subject: Renewal pricing: short-term price shelter + commit conversion proposal
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@novum.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@novum.ai
Date: 2027-11-21T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Renewal discussion + ask for short price shelter

Priya —

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We’re preparing our renewal request for Feb and wanted to surface two constraints up front: 1) our Q1 budget is locked and we need to avoid >10% list increases, and 2) we expect a 20% consumption increase if we go live on the new recommender in Jan.

Can Redwood provide a short-term price shelter (90 days) at current pricing while we finalize the commit for the new workload? If possible we’d like a path to convert existing retainer credits into committed capacity with a 6–12 month step-up. We attached our renewal RFP and high-level usage projection.

My ask: can you propose a conversion path (commit levels + credits) and a short price shelter so we avoid procurement delays? We’re aiming to sign by mid-Dec.

Best,
Elena
VP Product, Novum AI
--
Attachments: Novum_Renewal_RFP.pdf (pdf, 280 KB)
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@novum.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-21T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion + ask for short price shelter

Elena —

Thanks for the context and the RFP. We can absolutely structure a path that meets both objectives: short-term price shelter to protect against procurement timing, and an option to convert retainer credits into a stepped commit to support the Jan uplift.

High-level proposal (summary):
- 90-day price shelter at existing effective unit prices, starting on the renewal effective date;
- Option to convert up to 60% of current retainer credits into a committed capacity tranche (3-month ramp to full consumption) with a 6-month initial commitment and an auto step to 12 months if consumption stays >80% of committed;
- One-time bridging credit equal to 10% of the next quarter’s expected overage (applied as an invoice credit);
- Invoice timing: 50% of the first committed tranche upfront, remainder billed monthly;
- SLA/latency guard unchanged — we recommend the same model family; fallback policy included.

I’m looping Ben and Karthik for pricing sensitivity and to confirm what the bridging credit and invoice proration look like from a finance perspective. Monica — can you confirm success criteria for the Jan go-live and any onboarding credits we should bake into the amendment?

I’ll follow up with a scanned amendment (v1) and one-pager for procurement if this direction looks good.

Cheers,
Priya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
--
Attachments: RNWL_Amendment_proposal_v1.docx (docx, 75 KB)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-22T08:37:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion + ask for short price shelter

Priya —

Sketching numbers based on Novum's projection: if they convert 60% of retainer credits to commit (est. $120k/mo committed), we can offer:
- 90-day price shelter at current effective unit price (no uplift);
- Bridging credit: one-time $30k invoice credit (≈10% of Q1 overage estimate) applied upon signing;
- Discount band: 5% additional discount on committed units for the first 6 months if usage >= 85% of commit; otherwise revert to standard committed pricing;
- Payment terms: 50% upfront for the first tranche, 30-day net for remainder.

We should ensure procurement has the one-pager and a clean amendment. Karthik — any flags on the discount band or credit? Monica — confirm if CS can justify the 5% incentive from an onboarding success standpoint.

Ben
Head of Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Elena Ruiz <elena@novum.ai>
Date: 2027-11-23T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion + ask for short price shelter

Elena —

Thanks for the quick reply and the RFP. We’re okay to proceed with Priya/Ben’s outline. A few clarifications to keep procurement comfortable:
1) Price shelter window: starts on contract effective date and lasts 90 days. After that, committed pricing takes effect (with the 6→12 month step-up as discussed).
2) The bridging credit will be documented as a one-time invoice credit in the amendment; not a recurring discount.
3) Commit conversion mechanics: we will honor historical token conversions (retainer -> committed units) at the current effective rate, but the commitment term will be fixed at a minimum 6 months.

Elena — if that works, I’ll have Legal draft a short amendment referencing the RNWL_Amendment_proposal_v1 and the one-pager for procurement. We can also provide a DocuSign envelope and a single-sheet summary for finance.

-Karthik
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@novum.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, procurement@novum.ai
Date: 2027-11-24T14:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion + ask for short price shelter

Thanks — this looks good and addresses procurement's timing concern. Two quick asks before we move to Legal/DocuSign:
- Can the 90-day shelter be explicitly called out as "price hold" (procurement wants that language)?
- Can the bridging credit be split so 50% applies to the first invoice and 50% to the second, to help our cashflow team?

If you can adjust those two items, we’ll route the one-pager through procurement this week and aim to sign early Dec. Appreciate the flexibility — Jan go-live is important for both teams.

Elena
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@novum.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-26T17:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion + ask for short price shelter

Elena —

Appreciate the prompt feedback. We’ll make those two tweaks: label the 90-day period as a "Price Hold (90 days)" and split the $30k bridging credit into two $15k invoice credits applied to invoice 1 and invoice 2. I’ll update the RNWL_Amendment_proposal_v1 and push the one-pager and DocuSign envelope by EOD tomorrow.

Next actions:
- Priya to upload revised amendment + one-pager to Drive and send DocuSign link to procurement.
- Ben to confirm invoice credit mechanics with Finance ops for split application.
- Monica to confirm onboarding milestone metrics tied to the 5% incentive.

Target: procurement sign-off by 2027-12-08.

Thanks all —
Priya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
